body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

Three or four short sentences in all.

result:
crimson_scene: Cold soot clings to the iron brazier among the marble tombs of the Highborn Crypts. Only the pale ring of the hound's lantern keeps the clammy grave fog from swallowing your boots.
crimson_facts: Sir Marius Renathyr served a god of the morning and loved his sworn liege, King Viktor Denathria, like a brother. He rode a white charger named Dawn to hunt down every wicked thing on the road. Only the priestess Lethica could ever cool the terrible heat of his wrath.
crimson_nokindle: The kindling lies hidden near the tombs, though the fog has eaten the place from my mind. Search the stones again, for nothing is lost yet.
crimson_flame: Dry tinder catches with a sharp hiss, and a hungry crimson flame climbs the rusted bowl. The grave mist curdles thick around the pillars as ancient crypt guardians claw free of the marble to feed the fire.
crimson_hold: Hold your ground inside the lantern light and strike down every waking bone. Their husks must fall where the fire can see them die.
crimson_rite_prompt: The crimson fire wavers in the cold draft, waiting for you to feed it true words of the knight's road, his royal oath, or the woman who gentled his heart.
crimson_a_intro: You turn your voices toward the long roads Marius rode and the monsters he broke beneath Dawn's hooves. Each of you searches for the right words to honor his tireless blade.
crimson_a_okline: The crimson fire leaps high with a sound like ringing steel and galloping hooves. Your words strike true, warming the cold marble with the memory of his valor on the road.
crimson_a_missline: Your words ring hollow against the crypt stones, and the flame twists into a cruel puppet of a butcher trampling the weak under iron hooves. Every soul within the lantern circle flinches at the bitter laughter hissing from the mist.
crimson_b_intro: You speak now of his morning god and the brotherhood he swore to King Viktor Denathria. Each hero reaches for words worthy of an unbreakable oath.
crimson_b_okline: A clean golden heat swells inside the crimson flame as your tribute lands true. The fire remembers the morning light and the king he loved as blood.
crimson_b_missline: The tribute falters, and the spiteful dead twist the fire into the shape of a kneeling dog choking on a broken crown. A cold shudder runs through the party as the fog jeers at his ruined vow.
crimson_c_intro: You turn the rite toward the quiet priestess who alone could still the storm in his blood. Each of you reaches for a gentle truth to lay upon the coals.
crimson_c_okline: The jagged crimson tongues soften and rise steady and bright at the sound of your words. Even the bitter ash smells briefly of night-blooming herbs and quiet peace.
crimson_c_missline: The words stumble, and the shrouded spirits contort the flame into a weeping figure turning her back on a raving brute. Everyone who hears the wet, mocking sob from the brazier flinches back.
crimson_dies: The last grain of time runs out and the crimson fire gutters into cold black smoke. Yorgrim presses his spectral hand to the iron bowl, tearing a pale silver splinter from his own spirit to keep a single ember alive.
crimson_spent: I will feed more of my own marrow into the ash so fewer words are needed next time. My chains feel heavier now, and the stones are growing dim.
crimson_again: Gather your breath and try the rite once more, for no blame rests on your tongues.
crimson_done: The crimson beacon roars skyward in a pillar of hot blood-red light, driving the clammy shroud back from the Highborn Crypts. Far across the cemetery grounds, a single iron sconce catches fire high above the sepulcher doors.
crimson_thanks: You have given Marius back his morning light and his clean blade. Rest well, old friend, until the dawn returns.
crimson_all_lit: Five fires burn alongside my cold azure flame, and the heavy locks on the sepulcher doors have finally given way. Come back to the center, for our work lies below.
violet_scene: Wet bone-ash crunches underfoot around the cold iron brazier of the Cremation Gardens. Only the steady glow of the hound's lantern holds the pressing wall of mist at bay.
violet_facts: Lethica Nightborne wore the barn owl symbol of the Nightmother, goddess of night, healing, and motherhood. Sick pilgrims walked miles for her cures, though she hid her face behind a quiet mask until love found her. She alone could quiet Marius's fierce anger, and she gave him her whole heart in return.
violet_nokindle: The kindling is tucked somewhere among the urns, though my worn memory cannot hold the spot. Look again through the ash, for nothing is lost.
violet_flame: A spark takes hold in the damp tinder, sending a tall violet flame curling up from the iron bowl. The surrounding fog thickens like curdled milk as ash-caked guardians drag themselves up to be offered to the blaze.
violet_hold: Stay close within the lantern's ring and cut down whatever crawls from the ash. Spill their dust where the violet fire can watch them fall.
violet_rite_prompt: The violet blaze leans toward your voices, hungry for true remembrance of her healing hands, her devotion to Marius, or the hymns of her owl-winged goddess.
violet_a_intro: You turn the rite toward the fevers she cooled and the pilgrims who knelt at her door. Each of you searches for the clearest memory of her mercy.
violet_a_okline: The violet flame surges upward, shedding a warm scent of crushed lavender and clean linen across the damp stones. Your words land true, honoring the gentle hands that mended so many broken strangers.
violet_a_missline: Your words fall flat, and the shrouded dead twist the violet fire into a masked leech poisoning a begging child. Every person in the circle flinches from the shrill, cackling chorus that echoes through the gardens.
violet_b_intro: You turn your voices toward the masked woman who laid her armor down for a wrathful knight. Each hero reaches for words that honor the love she bore for Marius.
violet_b_okline: The violet fire leaps high and steady, braided with a warm thread of crimson light. Your words ring true, calling back the quiet touch that tamed a warrior's rage.
violet_b_missline: The tribute misses its mark, and spiteful spirits bend the flame into two lovers tearing at each other's throats behind iron masks. A sharp chill bites your skin as the watching mist hisses with delight.
violet_c_intro: You guide the rite toward the soft nocturnal prayers of the Nightmother and the white owl that watched over her shrine. Each of you reaches for the cadence of her old hymns.
